Moorea Coral Reef Productivity Analysis: Long-term Ecosystem Dynamics

Author

Nyssa Silbiger

Published

May 5, 2026

Introduction

This report analyzes long-term ecosystem dynamics at LTER Site 1 in Moorea, French Polynesia. We examine relationships between benthic community composition, environmental conditions, fish assemblages, and ecosystem metabolism over nearly two decades (2005-2025). The analysis integrates multiple datasets to understand how coral reef ecosystems are responding to environmental change.

Data

1. Temperature Data

Extract yearly average and maximum daily temperature values from the backreef temperature time series.

Code 
# Read and process temperature data
Temp_LTER1 <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "MCR_LTER02_BTM_Backreef_Forereef_20251114.csv")) |>
  filter(reef_type_code == "Backreef")

# Calculate daily means, then yearly statistics (optimized with single pass)
Mean_year_Temp <- Temp_LTER1 |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time_local)) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(daily_temp = mean(temperature_c, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Year = year(date)) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    Mean_temp = mean(daily_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max_temp = max(daily_temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Save processed data
write_csv(Mean_year_Temp, here("Data", "InSituTemp.csv"))

# Quick summary
summary(Mean_year_Temp)

2. Nutrient Data

Process macroalgae tissue nitrogen content and water column nutrients, using tissue N to impute missing water column data.

Code 
# Turbinaria %N data (tissue nitrogen as nutrient proxy)
Turb <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "MCR_LTER_Macroalgal_CHN_2005_to_2024_20250616.csv")) |>
  filter(
    Habitat == "Backreef",
    Genus == "Turbinaria",
    Site == "LTER_1",
    !is.na(N)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    N_percent = mean(N, na.rm = TRUE),
    C_percent = mean(C, na.rm = TRUE),
    CN = mean(CN_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(Turb, here("Data", "Turb_mean.csv"))

# Water column nutrients (bimonthly surveys 2005-2018)
water <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "WaterColumnN.csv")) |>
  mutate(
    Date = mdy(Date),
    Year = year(Date)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(across(Phosphate:Nitrite_and_Nitrate,  \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(Site = "LTER 1")

write_csv(water, here("Data", "Water_N_mean.csv"))

# Impute water N+N from tissue N using linear model
AllNutrients <- Turb |>
  full_join(water, by = "Year") |>
  arrange(Year)

# Model and predict
modN <- lm(Nitrite_and_Nitrate ~ N_percent, data = AllNutrients)
AllNutrients$NN_impute <- predict(modN, newdata = AllNutrients)

# Model summary
cat("\nNutrient imputation model (Nitrite+Nitrate ~ Tissue %N):\n")

3. Benthic Cover Data

Calculate percent cover for functional groups from benthic transect surveys.

Code 
# Read and classify benthic data
BenthicCover_Algae <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "MCR_LTER_Annual_Survey_Benthic_Cover_20251009.csv")) |>
  filter(Habitat == "Backreef")

# Create functional group classifications (vectorized)
Benthic_summary_Algae <- BenthicCover_Algae |>
  rename(name = Taxonomy_Substrate_Functional_Group) |>
  mutate(
    name = case_when(
      name %in% c(
        "Amansia rhodantha", "Turbinaria ornata", "Dictyota sp.", "Halimeda sp.",
        "Galaxaura sp.", "Liagora ceranoides", "Cyanophyta", "Halimeda minima",
        "Amphiroa fragilissima", "Caulerpa serrulata", "Corallimorpharia",
        "Dictyota friabilis", "Galaxaura rugosa", "Cladophoropsis membranacea",
        "Galaxaura filamentosa", "Halimeda discoidea", "Peyssonnelia inamoena",
        "Caulerpa racemosa", "Valonia ventricosa", "Actinotrichia fragilis",
        "Dictyota bartayresiana", "Microdictyon umbilicatum", "Halimeda distorta",
        "Halimeda incrassata", "Halimeda macroloba", "Dictyota implexa",
        "Gelidiella acerosa", "Dictyosphaeria cavernosa", "Valonia aegagropila",
        "Microdictyon okamurae", "Halimeda opuntia", "Dichotomaria obtusata",
        "Chlorodesmis fastigiata", "Phyllodictyon anastomosans", "Phormidium sp.",
        "Cladophoropsis luxurians", "Sargassum pacificum", "Chnoospora implexa",
        "Halimeda taenicola", "Boodlea kaeneana", "Padina boryana",
        "Coelothrix irregularis", "Gelidiella sp.", "Hydroclathrus clathratus",
        "Dictyota divaricata", "Hypnea spinella", "Dichotomaria marginata",
        "Sporolithon sp.", "Chaetomorpha antennina", "Asparagopsis taxiformis"
      ) ~ "Fleshy Macroalgae",
      name %in% c(
        "Algal Turf", "Damselfish Turf", "Coral Rubble",
        "Lobophora variegata", "Shell Debris", "Bare Space"
      ) ~ "Turf/Cyanobacteria",
      name %in% c(
        "Peyssonnelia bornetii", "Peyssonnelia sp.",
        "Sponge", "Tridacna sp.", "No data"
      ) ~ "Sand",
      TRUE ~ name
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, Site, name) |>
  summarise(
    total_cover = sum(Percent_Cover, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_cover = 100 * total_cover / 5000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(Site = str_replace_all(Site, "_", " "))

write_csv(Benthic_summary_Algae, here("Data", "Benthic_summary_algae.csv"))

# Calculate total calcifiers and living cover
Total_Calc <- Benthic_summary_Algae |>
  filter(name %in% c("Coral", "Crustose Corallines")) |>
  group_by(Year, Site) |>
  reframe(total_Calc = sum(mean_cover))

TotalLiving <- Benthic_summary_Algae |>
  filter(name %in% c("Coral", "Crustose Corallines", "Fleshy Macroalgae")) |>
  group_by(Year, Site) |>
  summarise(
    mean_alive = sum(mean_cover),
    mean_fleshy = sum(mean_cover[name == "Fleshy Macroalgae"], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_coral = sum(mean_cover[name == "Coral"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

4. Fish Biomass Data

Process fish survey data by trophic groups.

Code 
# Read and process fish data
fish <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "MCR_LTER_Annual_Fish_Survey_20250324.csv"))

# Process by trophic groups (optimized filtering)
fish_summary <- fish |>
  filter(
    Site == "LTER_1",
    Habitat == "Backreef",
    Biomass < 8000, # Remove outlier sharks
    Biomass >= 0 # Remove negative (missing) values
  ) |>
  mutate(
    trophic_new = case_when(
      Fine_Trophic %in% c("Brusher", "Browser", "Excavator", "Scraper") ~ "Herbivores",
      Fine_Trophic == "Corallivore" ~ "Corallivore",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, trophic_new) |>
  summarise(
    fish_g_m2 = sum(Biomass, na.rm = TRUE) / 1200, # 4 transects × 300 m²
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(fish_summary, here("Data", "fish_summary.csv"))

5. Primary Production Processing

Process raw production data and extract Pmax and Rd using Bayesian photosynthesis-irradiance curves.

Code 
# Read all QC PP files efficiently
filedir <- here("Data", "raw_data", "QC_PP")
files <- dir(path = filedir, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)

All_PP_data <- files |>
  set_names() |>
  map_df(read_csv, .id = "filename", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(DateTime = mdy_hm(DateTime))

# Unit conversion and data cleaning (optimized)
All_PP_data <- All_PP_data |>
  mutate(
    # Convert 2007-2014 from g O2/m2/h to mmol O2/m2/h
    across(
      c(UP_Oxy, DN_Oxy, PP),
      ~ if_else(DateTime < ymd_hms("2014-04-01 00:00:00"), (.x / 32) * 1000, .x)
    ),
    Date = as_date(DateTime),
    DielDateTime = DateTime + hours(12),
    DielDate = as_date(DielDateTime),
    Year = year(DateTime)
  ) |>
  filter(!Date %in% mdy(c("5/27/2011", "5/28/2011", "1/21/2014", "05/25/2024")))

# Keep only complete 24-hour datasets
complete_dates <- All_PP_data |>
  count(DielDate) |>
  filter(n == 24)

All_PP_data <- complete_dates |>
  left_join(All_PP_data, by = "DielDate")

# Calculate GP and environmental averages
Daily_R <- All_PP_data |>
  group_by(Year, Season, DielDate) |>
  summarise(R_average = mean(PP[PAR == 0], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

All_PP_data <- All_PP_data |>
  left_join(Daily_R, by = c("Year", "Season", "DielDate")) |>
  mutate(
    GP = if_else(PAR == 0, NA_real_, PP - R_average),
    GP = if_else(GP < 0, NA_real_, GP),
    Temperature_mean = (UP_Temp + DN_Temp) / 2,
    Flow_mean = (UP_Velocity_mps + DN_Velocity_mps) / 2
  )

# Calculate yearly averages
Year_Averages_PP <- All_PP_data |>
  mutate(
    NP = PP,
    R = if_else(PP < 0, PP, NA_real_)
  ) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    NP_mean = mean(NP, na.rm = TRUE),
    NP_SE = sd(NP, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    NP_max = max(NP, na.rm = TRUE),
    GP_mean = mean(GP, na.rm = TRUE),
    GP_SE = sd(GP, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    R_mean = mean(R, na.rm = TRUE),
    R_SE = sd(R, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    Temperature_mean = mean(Temperature_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    Flow_mean = mean(Flow_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    PAR_mean = mean(PAR[PAR > 0], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

Bayesian Photosynthesis-Irradiance (PI) Curve Analysis

We fit a Bayesian non-linear model to extract photosynthetic parameters (alpha, Pmax, and Rd) for each year. The model uses a rectangular hyperbola:

\[PP = \frac{\alpha \cdot P_{max} \cdot PAR}{\alpha \cdot PAR + P_{max}} + R_d\]

where: - \(\alpha\) = initial slope (photosynthetic efficiency) - \(P_{max}\) = maximum photosynthetic capacity - \(R_d\) = dark respiration (ecosystem respiration) - \(PAR\) = photosynthetically active radiation

Code 
# Bayesian PI curves to extract light-independent Pmax and Rd
LTER1_Pnet <- All_PP_data |>
  mutate(
    tempc = Temperature_mean,
    Flowmean = Flow_mean,
    flow_log = log(Flowmean),
    UPDN = as.factor(UPDN),
    Year = as.factor(Year)
  )

# Fit Bayesian nonlinear model
fit1_f <- brm(
  bf(
    PP ~ ((alpha * Pmax * PAR) / (alpha * PAR + Pmax)) + Rd,
    nl = TRUE,
    alpha ~ 0 + Year,
    Pmax ~ 0 + Year,
    Rd ~ 0 + Year
  ) + student(),
  data = LTER1_Pnet,
  set_rescor(FALSE),
  prior = c(
    prior(normal(0.1, 10), nlpar = "alpha", lb = 0),
    prior(normal(-100, 10), nlpar = "Rd", ub = 0),
    prior(normal(100, 10), nlpar = "Pmax", lb = 0)
  ),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 20),
  cores = 3,
  chains = 3,
  seed = 223,
  iter = 8000,
  warmup = 2000
)

# Extract Pmax and Rd coefficients
names <- rownames(fixef(fit1_f))
coefficients <- as_tibble(fixef(fit1_f)) |>
  mutate(params = names)

PRValues <- coefficients |>
  separate(params, sep = "_", into = c("param_type", "yearname"), remove = FALSE) |>
  filter(param_type %in% c("Pmax", "Rd")) |>
  separate(yearname, sep = "r", into = c("y", "year")) |>
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year)) |>
  select(Year = year, Estimate, param_type) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = param_type, values_from = Estimate)

# Combine with raw averages
Year_Averages_PP <- Year_Averages_PP |>
  full_join(PRValues, by = "Year") |>
  mutate(Rd = -Rd) # Make Rd positive

# Calculate Bayesian R²
pi_curve_r2 <- median(bayes_R2(fit1_f)[, 1])
cat(sprintf("\nPhotosynthesis-Irradiance Curve Model:\n"))

Photosynthesis-Irradiance Curve Model:
Code 
cat(sprintf("  Bayesian R²: %.3f\n", pi_curve_r2))

6. Integrate All Datasets

Code 
# Read processed data files
Year_Averages_PP <- read_csv(here("Data", "Year_Averages_PP.csv"))
Turb <- read_csv(here("Data", "Turb_mean.csv"))
water <- read_csv(here("Data", "Water_N_mean.csv"))
insitu_temp <- read_csv(here("Data", "InSituTemp.csv"))

fish_trophic <- read_csv(here("Data", "fish_summary.csv")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = trophic_new, values_from = fish_g_m2) |>
  select(-Other)

Benthic_summary_Algae <- read_csv(here("Data", "Benthic_summary_algae.csv"))

# Create integrated dataset
Year_Averages <- Year_Averages_PP |>
  full_join(TotalLiving |> filter(Site == "LTER 1"), by = "Year") |>
  full_join(water) |>
  full_join(Turb, by = "Year") |>
  full_join(insitu_temp, by = "Year") |>
  full_join(fish_trophic, by = "Year") |>
  mutate(log_coral = log(mean_coral)) |>
  filter(Year < 2026) |>
  arrange(Year)

Methods

Photosynthesis-Irradiance Curve Analysis

Annual values of maximum photosynthetic capacity (Pmax) and ecosystem respiration (Rd) were extracted from a Bayesian nonlinear model fit to 2,928 net O₂ flux measurements using the brms package (Bürkner 2017) and Stan (Carpenter et al. 2017). We used the rectangular hyperbola:

\[\mathrm{PP} = \frac{\alpha \cdot P_{\max} \cdot \mathrm{PAR}}{\alpha \cdot \mathrm{PAR} + P_{\max}} + R_d\]

where PP is net community production, PAR is photosynthetically active radiation, and α is photosynthetic efficiency. Year-specific parameters (α, Pmax, Rd) were estimated simultaneously from all deployments. A Student-t likelihood accommodated measurement outliers. Priors were weakly informative: α ~ Normal\(_+\)(0.1, 10); Pmax ~ Normal\(_+\)(100, 10); Rd ~ Normal\(_-\)(−100, 10). Three chains ran for 8,000 iterations (2,000 warmup) at adapt_delta = 0.95. Posterior Rd values were multiplied by −1 to express ecosystem respiration as positive rates.

Temporal Trend Analysis

We estimated standardised temporal trends for 10 ecosystem variables (coral cover, fleshy macroalgae, corallivore biomass, herbivore biomass, algal nitrogen content, ecosystem respiration, Pmax, net ecosystem production, maximum temperature, nitrate+nitrite) using independent Bayesian linear regression models (Variable ~ Year, default brms priors) on z-scored data. The slope posterior (change per standardised year) was used to assess direction and magnitude of each trend. Effects were considered directional when the 95% credible interval excluded zero. Bayesian R² (Gelman et al. 2019) is reported as the posterior median. Absolute percent change was calculated between the first and last non-missing observations on the original scale.

Correlation Analysis

Pearson correlations among all major ecosystem variables were computed and visualised as a mixed correlation matrix (upper triangle: ellipses scaled by correlation strength; lower triangle: numeric values; diagonal: variable names). Significance was assessed using two-tailed t-tests; variables were ordered by hierarchical clustering of the correlation matrix.

Structural Equation Modeling

To evaluate simultaneous causal pathways among ecosystem components, we fit a Bayesian multivariate SEM in brms with residual correlations disabled (set_rescor = FALSE). The directed acyclic graph (DAG) was motivated by ecological theory and temporal precedence, comprising eight response equations:

# Equation
1 Temperature ~ Year
2 log(coral cover) | trunc(ub = 3.39) ~ temperature + yearresid
3 log(ecosystem respiration) ~ log(coral cover) + temperature
4 log(fleshy macroalgae) | trunc(ub = 2.26) ~ log(coral cover)
5 log(Pmax) ~ log(coral cover) + temperature + log(ecosystem respiration)
6 corallivore biomass ~ log(coral cover)
7 herbivore biomass ~ log(fleshy macroalgae)
8 log(nitrogen content) ~ log(ecosystem respiration)

All continuous responses were log-transformed and z-score standardised before modelling. The yearresid predictor is the residual of calendar year regressed on maximum annual temperature, capturing non-thermal secular coral decline. Cover responses were upper-truncated at the z-log scale equivalent of 100% cover to respect the biological ceiling; truncation values (3.39 for coral, 2.26 for fleshy algae) were verified to back-transform to exactly 100%.

Missing predictor values (ecosystem respiration and temperature as predictors of Pmax; ecosystem respiration as predictor of N content) were handled via brms integrated missing-data imputation (mi() syntax). Priors were weakly informative: regression coefficients ~ Normal(0, 2); intercepts ~ Normal(0, 2); residual SDs ~ Normal\(_+\)(0, 0.25) for the temperature sub-model and Normal\(_+\)(0, 2) otherwise. Three chains ran for 10,000 iterations (5,000 warmup) with adapt_delta = 0.99 and max_treedepth = 15. Convergence was assessed via Rhat (< 1.01 for all parameters), bulk and tail effective sample sizes (> 1,000), and posterior predictive checks.

Parsimonious (reduced) SEM

A reduced model was fit by removing three pathways whose 95% credible intervals included zero in the full model: Temperature → Respiration (direct), Temperature → Pmax (direct), and Coral → Pmax (direct). All retained coefficients were stable between full and reduced models (within 0.02 SD). The reduced model is used for all ecosystem projections.

Direct and indirect temperature effects

Total standardised effects of temperature on each ecosystem variable were decomposed into direct paths and indirect paths (products of coefficients along each chain through the DAG) using all 15,000 post-warmup draws. Indirect effects were computed as the product of relevant path coefficients; for example, the indirect effect on respiration was β(Temp→Coral) × β(Coral→Rd). Total effects are the sum across all contributing paths. An effect was considered credible if its 95% CI excluded zero.

Ecosystem Projections

CMIP6 climate scenario projections (to 2100)

To project ecosystem trajectories under realistic climate forcing, monthly sea surface temperature (tos, variable sea_surface_temperature) for the Moorea grid cell (~17.5°S, 149.8°W) was obtained from ten coupled CMIP6 ScenarioMIP models — ACCESS-CM2 (Bi et al. 2020), BCC-CSM2-MR (Wu et al. 2019), EC-Earth3 (Döscher et al. 2022), GFDL-ESM4 (Dunne et al. 2020), IPSL-CM6A-LR (Boucher et al. 2020), MIROC6 (Tatebe et al. 2019), MPI-ESM1-2-LR (Müller et al. 2018), MRI-ESM2-0 (Yukimoto et al. 2019), NorESM2-LM (Seland et al. 2020), and UKESM1-0-LL (Sellar et al. 2019) (Eyring et al. 2016) — downloaded from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (projections-cmip6 dataset; Copernicus Climate Change Service 2023; https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/projections-cmip6; DOI: 10.24381/cds.c866074c) via the ecmwfr R package (Hufkens et al. 2019; https://bluegreen-labs.github.io/ecmwfr/). Data were requested for 2015–2100 under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways: SSP1-2.6 (strong mitigation, ~1.5–2°C global warming by 2100), SSP2-4.5 (intermediate stabilisation), and SSP5-8.5 (high emissions, ~4–5°C warming; O’Neill et al. 2016; Riahi et al. 2017). A historical baseline (1950–2014) was obtained from the same models and stitched to the SSP series at 2015. All data were spatially subsetted to a 3° bounding box centred on Moorea (~16°S to ~19°S, ~148°E to ~151°E) and the nearest grid cell to the LTER Site 1 backreef location was extracted. Monthly tos values were converted from Kelvin to Celsius where necessary (units check per NetCDF metadata), aggregated to annual maxima per model-year, and ensemble p10, median, and p90 quantiles were computed across models for each scenario-year.

Each model’s annual maximum SST series was delta bias-corrected to the observed MCR 2005–2025 annual maximum temperature mean (additive shift per model, computed over the 2005–2025 overlap window combining the historical run for 2005–2014 and the SSP run for 2015–2025). Using location-specific coupled-model SST eliminates the need for an air-to-SST offset correction and provides warming rates directly relevant to the reef environment. All ten models were confirmed available on the CDS for the projections-cmip6 dataset with the sea_surface_temperature variable.

Projections used a two-phase approach. For the historical period (2005–2025), observed annual z-scores from the fitted dataset were used directly for each ecosystem variable where data were available, replacing the sequential SEM chain prediction; the SEM chain was retained only for 2005 (pre-data) and for variable–year combinations with missing observations. This ensures the historical projection lines track the observed data rather than the amplified sequential predictions of the SEM chain. For the projection period (2026–2100), a delta method anchored the projection to the 2025 observed ecosystem state: only the change in temperature from the scenario’s CMIP6 2025 value was propagated forward through the SEM path coefficients, starting from the actual 2025 coral cover (6.8%), ecosystem respiration (28.5 mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹), fleshy macroalgae (14.7%), and Pmax (113.3 mmol O₂ m⁻² hr⁻¹). Algal N content in 2025 was imputed from the observed Rd via the SEM regression (N_percent was not measured in 2025). This approach was used for all nine scenario × percentile combinations (3,000 posterior draws each, totalling 27,000 projection runs). The inner uncertainty ribbon on projection figures represents the SEM posterior 95% credible interval using the ensemble median temperature; the outer ribbon represents the CMIP6 multi-model p10–p90 spread at the SEM posterior median, thereby separating climate-forcing uncertainty from model-parameter uncertainty. For the historical period (2005–2014), the outer uncertainty ribbon shows the inter-model p10–p90 spread across the ten bias-corrected CMIP6 historical runs.

Software and Reproducibility

Key packages: tidyverse 2.0 (Wickham et al. 2019), brms 2.21 (Bürkner 2017), tidybayes 3.0 (Kay 2023), patchwork 1.2 (Pedersen 2024), ggraph 2.1 and igraph 1.6 (Csárdi & Nepusz 2006), httr2 (Wickham 2023), zoo (Zeileis & Grothendieck 2005), cowplot (Wilke 2024), ecmwfr (Hufkens et al. 2019; https://bluegreen-labs.github.io/ecmwfr/), ncdf4 (Pierce 2024). Stan 2.32 served as the computational backend. CMIP6 SST data were accessed from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/datasets/projections-cmip6; DOI: 10.24381/cds.c866074c). All analysis code and processed data are available at [INSERT REPOSITORY DOI]; MCR LTER raw data are publicly archived through the EDI Data Portal (https://edirepository.org).

Temporal Trends

Assess standardized change per year using Bayesian linear models.

Code 
# Create standardized dataset
std_data <- Year_Averages |>
  select(
    mean_coral, mean_fleshy, Pmax, Rd, N_percent,
    Herbivores, Corallivore, NP_mean, Max_temp, GP_mean,
    Nitrite_and_Nitrate, Phosphate
  ) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)))) |>
  bind_cols(Year_Averages |> select(Year))

# Fit Bayesian models for each variable and extract R²
fit_temporal_model <- function(response_var, param_name) {
  form <- as.formula(paste(response_var, "~ Year"))
  mod <- brm(form, data = std_data, silent = 2, refresh = 0, seed = 223)
  
  # Extract posterior samples
  post <- as_tibble(as.matrix(mod)) |>
    select(Year = b_Year) |>
    mutate(Parameter = param_name)
  
  # Calculate Bayesian R²
  r2 <- median(bayes_R2(mod)[, 1])
  
  # Store model for later R² extraction
  list(posterior = post, model = mod, r2 = r2, param = param_name)
}

# Fit all models
temporal_models <- list(
  fit_temporal_model("mean_coral", "% Coral Cover"),
  fit_temporal_model("mean_fleshy", "% Macroalgae Cover"),
  fit_temporal_model("Corallivore", "Corallivore"),
  fit_temporal_model("Herbivores", "Herbivore/bioeroding fish"),
  fit_temporal_model("N_percent", "%N Content"),
  fit_temporal_model("Rd", "Ecosystem Respiration"),
  fit_temporal_model("Pmax", "Maximum Photosynthetic Capacity"),
  fit_temporal_model("NP_mean", "Net Ecosystem Production"),
  fit_temporal_model("Max_temp", "Max Temperature"),
  fit_temporal_model("Nitrite_and_Nitrate", "Nitrate + Nitrite")
)

# Extract posteriors for plotting
temporal_results <- temporal_models |>
  map_df(~.x$posterior)

# Print R² values
cat("\n=== Temporal Trend Model Performance (Bayesian R²) ===\n\n")

# ── Nature-ready base theme (7 pt, classic, no gridlines) ──────────────────
theme_nature <- function(base_size = 7) {
  theme_classic(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text             = element_text(family = "noto"),
      axis.text        = element_text(size = base_size, color = "black"),
      axis.title       = element_text(size = base_size + 0.5),
      axis.line        = element_line(linewidth = 0.35, color = "black"),
      axis.ticks       = element_line(linewidth = 0.35, color = "black"),
      strip.background = element_blank(),
      strip.text       = element_text(size = 6.5, face = "plain", color = "grey20"),
      panel.spacing    = unit(0.5, "lines"),
      legend.position  = "none",
      plot.tag         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9)
    )
}

col_inc <- "#E64B35"   # NPG red  — increasing
col_dec <- "#4DBBD5"   # NPG teal — decreasing

# ── Summarise posterior slopes (order + color mapping) ─────────────────────

# ── Back-transform fitted values and raw data to original scales ────────────

# ── Extract fitted values + raw data from each Bayesian model ───────────────
get_time_series <- function(model_obj) {
  mod      <- model_obj$model
  param    <- model_obj$param
  resp_var <- as.character(formula(mod)$formula)[2]
  year_seq <- tibble(Year = seq(min(std_data$Year), max(std_data$Year), by = 0.5))
  fitted_df <- fitted(mod, newdata = year_seq) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    bind_cols(year_seq) |>
    mutate(Parameter = param)
  raw_df <- std_data |>
    select(Year, value = all_of(resp_var)) |>
    mutate(Parameter = param)
  list(fitted = fitted_df, raw = raw_df)
}

all_series <- map(temporal_models, get_time_series)

fitted_all <- map_df(all_series, ~.x$fitted) |>
  left_join(slope_summary |> select(Parameter, direction), by = "Parameter") |>
  left_join(scale_params |> select(Parameter, mu, sd, label), by = "Parameter") |>
  mutate(
    Estimate_orig = Estimate * sd + mu,
    Q2.5_orig     = Q2.5    * sd + mu,
    Q97.5_orig    = Q97.5   * sd + mu,
    label = factor(label, levels = label_levels)
  )

raw_all <- map_df(all_series, ~.x$raw) |>
  left_join(slope_summary |> select(Parameter, direction), by = "Parameter") |>
  left_join(scale_params |> select(Parameter, mu, sd, label), by = "Parameter") |>
  mutate(
    value_orig = value * sd + mu,
    label = factor(label, levels = label_levels)
  )

# ── Bayesian R² annotations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
r2_df <- map_df(temporal_models, ~tibble(Parameter = .x$param, r2 = .x$r2)) |>
  left_join(scale_params |> select(Parameter, label), by = "Parameter") |>
  mutate(
    label    = factor(label, levels = label_levels),
    r2_label = paste0("R\u00b2 = ", round(r2, 2))
  )

# ── Panel b: Small-multiple time series on original scale ───────────────────
panel_b <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = fitted_all,
    aes(x = Year, ymin = Q2.5_orig, ymax = Q97.5_orig, fill = direction),
    alpha = 0.18
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = fitted_all,
    aes(x = Year, y = Estimate_orig, color = direction),
    linewidth = 0.55
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = raw_all,
    aes(x = Year, y = value_orig),
    size = 0.85, alpha = 0.70, shape = 16, color = "grey25"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = r2_df,
    aes(label = r2_label),
    x = -Inf, y = Inf,
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.4,
    size = 1.8, color = "grey45", fontface = "italic", family = "noto"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = c("Increasing" = col_inc, "Decreasing" = col_dec)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Increasing" = col_inc, "Decreasing" = col_dec)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2008, 2014, 2020)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = NULL, tag = "b") +
  theme_nature() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 5.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5.5)
  )

Model Performance Summary: The Bayesian temporal trend models showed varying explanatory power across ecosystem variables. Temperature and coral cover trends had the highest R² values (>0.5), indicating highly predictable linear trajectories over time. Metabolic variables (Pmax, Rd, NP) showed moderate explanatory power (R² = 0.2-0.5), reflecting both directional trends and substantial year-to-year variability. Fish biomass trends had lower R² values, suggesting additional drivers beyond benthic habitat changes influence these populations.

Correlation Analysis

Structural Equation Modeling

Fit a Bayesian SEM to understand causal pathways among ecosystem components.

Code 
# Calculate year residuals (disturbances beyond temperature)
yearresid <- resid(lm(Year ~ Max_temp, data = Year_Averages, na.action = na.pass))

# Prepare scaled SEM data
semdata2 <- Year_Averages |>
  mutate(
    logfleshy = log(mean_fleshy),
    logrd = log(Rd),
    logpmax = log(Pmax),
    logproducers = log(mean_alive),
    N_percent = log(N_percent),
    yearresid = yearresid
  ) |>
  select(
    Year, meancoral = mean_coral, logproducers, meanfleshy = mean_fleshy,
    temperature = Max_temp, flow = Flow_mean, Npercent = N_percent,
    logrd, logpmax, logcoral = log_coral, logfleshy, Corallivore,
    herbs = Herbivores, yearresid
  ) |>
  drop_na(logcoral) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))
Code 
# Define SEM structure
bf_temp <- bf(temperature | mi() ~ 1 + Year)
bf_coraltemp <- bf(logcoral | trunc(ub = 3.39) ~ 1 + temperature + yearresid)
bf_logpmax <- bf(logpmax | mi() ~ 1 + logcoral + mi(temperature) + mi(logrd)) ####
bf_logrd <- bf(logrd | mi() ~ 1 + logcoral + mi(temperature))
bf_herbs <- bf(herbs | mi() ~ 1 + logfleshy)
bf_corallivore <- bf(Corallivore | mi() ~ 1 + logcoral)
bf_fleshy <- bf(logfleshy | trunc(ub = 2.26) ~ logcoral)
bf_nutrients <- bf(Npercent | mi() ~ 1 + mi(logrd))

# Fit full SEM
brms_sem_full <- brm(
  bf_temp + bf_coraltemp + bf_logrd + bf_herbs + bf_corallivore +
    bf_nutrients + bf_fleshy + bf_logpmax + set_rescor(FALSE),
  data = semdata2,
  chains = 3,
  iter = 10000,
  warmup = 5000,
  seed = 11,
  sample_prior = "no",
  prior = c(
    set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b"),
    set_prior("normal(0, 0.25)", resp = "temperature", class = "sigma", lb = 0),
    set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept")
  ),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15),
  family = gaussian(),
  silent = 2,
  refresh = 0
)

Code 
pos_col  <- "#1565C0"
neg_col  <- "#B71C1C"
nsig_col <- "#AAAAAA"

# N Stock elevated above the Rd–Pmax horizontal line (y=5.0 vs Rd/Pmax at y=4.0)
# Rd→Pmax is a straight horizontal beneath N; Rd→N is a short diagonal upward
# All edges are straight segments — no curves at all
# Rows compressed: ecosystem at y=4.0, community at y=2.0, gap = 2.0 units
dag_nodes <- tribble(
  ~id,           ~label,                    ~x,    ~y,    ~fill,       ~border,
  "Year",        "Year",                    0.4,   3.5,   "white",     "#888888",
  "Temp",        "Temperature",             2.0,   3.0,   "white",     "#888888",
  "Coral",       "Coral\nCover",            3.8,   3.0,   "#E8F5E9",   "#2E7D32",
  # Ecosystem function: Rd and Pmax in horizontal row; N elevated above
  "Rd",          "Ecosystem\nRespiration",  5.6,   4.0,   "#EDE7F6",   "#4527A0",
  "N",           "N\nStock",               7.4,   5.0,   "#FFF8E1",   "#E65100",
  "Pmax",        "Ecosystem\nPmax",         9.2,   4.0,   "#EDE7F6",   "#4527A0",
  # Community composition row
  "Algae",       "Fleshy\nAlgae",           5.6,   2.0,   "#E8F5E9",   "#2E7D32",
  "Herbs",       "Herbivore\nFish",         7.4,   2.0,   "#E3F2FD",   "#0D47A1",
  "Corallivore", "Corallivore\nFish",       9.2,   2.0,   "#E3F2FD",   "#0D47A1"
)

dag_edges <- tribble(
  ~from,   ~to,           ~est,   ~sig,  ~loff_x, ~loff_y,
  "Year",  "Temp",        0.465,  TRUE,   0.28,    0.18,
  "Temp",  "Coral",      -0.549,  TRUE,   0.00,    0.24,
  "Temp",  "Rd",          0.214,  FALSE, -0.35,    0.24,
  "Temp",  "Pmax",       -0.158,  FALSE, -0.75,   -0.22,
  "Coral", "Rd",          1.080,  TRUE,  -0.08,    0.24,
  "Coral", "Algae",      -0.914,  TRUE,  -0.08,   -0.24,
  "Coral", "Corallivore", 0.645,  TRUE,   0.38,   -0.20,
  "Coral", "Pmax",       -0.353,  FALSE,  0.38,    0.20,
  "Rd",    "N",           0.623,  TRUE,  -0.18,    0.22,   # short diagonal up-right
  "Rd",    "Pmax",        0.819,  TRUE,   0.00,    0.24,   # straight horizontal below N
  "Algae", "Herbs",       0.711,  TRUE,   0.00,    0.24    # straight horizontal
) |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(est >= 0, "pos", "neg"), abs_est = abs(est)) |>
  left_join(dag_nodes |> select(id, x, y) |> rename(from = id, x0 = x, y0 = y), by = "from") |>
  left_join(dag_nodes |> select(id, x, y) |> rename(to   = id, x1 = x, y1 = y), by = "to") |>
  mutate(mx = (x0 + x1) / 2, my = (y0 + y1) / 2, lbl = sprintf("%.2f", est))

# All edges are straight — no geom_curve needed
dag_arr <- arrow(length = unit(3.0, "mm"), type = "closed")

ggplot() +
  # Faint region backgrounds
  annotate("rect", xmin = 4.8, xmax = 10.0, ymin = 3.2, ymax = 5.65,
           fill = "#EDE7F6", alpha = 0.18, color = NA) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 4.8, xmax = 10.0, ymin = 1.2, ymax = 2.75,
           fill = "#E3F2FD", alpha = 0.18, color = NA) +
  # Region labels
  annotate("text", x = 10.12, y = 4.5, label = "Ecosystem\nfunction",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.6, color = "#6A1B9A", fontface = "italic", lineheight = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 10.12, y = 2.0, label = "Community\ncomposition",
           hjust = 0, size = 2.6, color = "#1565C0", fontface = "italic", lineheight = 0.9) +
  # Significant edges
  geom_segment(data = filter(dag_edges,  sig),
    aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1, color = direction, linewidth = abs_est),
    alpha = 0.82, arrow = dag_arr, lineend = "butt") +
  # Non-significant edges — reduced alpha to de-emphasise
  geom_segment(data = filter(dag_edges, !sig),
    aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1, linewidth = abs_est),
    color = nsig_col, alpha = 0.45, arrow = dag_arr, lineend = "butt") +
  geom_label(data = filter(dag_edges,  sig),
    aes(x = mx + loff_x, y = my + loff_y, label = lbl, color = direction),
    size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", fill = "white",
    label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.07, "lines"), show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_label(data = filter(dag_edges, !sig),
    aes(x = mx + loff_x, y = my + loff_y, label = lbl),
    color = nsig_col, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", fill = "white",
    label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.07, "lines"), show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Node boxes
  {lapply(seq_len(nrow(dag_nodes)), function(i) {
    nd <- dag_nodes[i, ]
    geom_label(data = nd, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
               fill = nd$fill, color = nd$border, size = 3.0,
               fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.9, label.size = 0.65,
               label.padding = unit(0.38, "lines"), label.r = unit(4, "pt"),
               show.legend = FALSE)
  })} +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("pos" = pos_col, "neg" = neg_col),
                     labels = c("pos" = "Positive", "neg" = "Negative"),
                     name = "Effect direction") +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.6, 2.8), guide = "none") +
  labs(caption = "Standardized β on arrows  ·  gray = 95% CI crosses zero") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.caption    = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "grey55", size = 9, margin = margin(t = 6)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title    = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.text     = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin     = margin(8, 10, 6, 10)
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.1, 11.8), ylim = c(1.35, 5.75))

SEM Path Coefficients

Code 
# Extract and format path coefficients
gp_edges <- as_tibble(fixef(brms_sem_full)) |>
  mutate(coef = rownames(fixef(brms_sem_full))) |>
  separate(col = coef, into = c("resp", "pred")) |>
  filter(pred != "Intercept") |>
  rename(est = Estimate, lo = `Q2.5`, hi = `Q97.5`) |>
  mutate(sig = if_else(sign(lo) == sign(hi), 1, 0.5)) |>
  mutate(resp = case_when(
    resp == "temperature" ~ "Temperature",
    resp == "logfleshy" ~ "Fleshy Macroalgae",
    resp == "logpmax" ~ "Ecosystem Pmax",
    resp == "logrd" ~ "Ecosystem Rd",
    resp == "herbs" ~ "Herbivorous Fish",
    resp == "Corallivore" ~ "Corallivore Fish",
    resp == "logcoral" ~ "Coral",
    resp == "Npercent" ~ "N stock"
  )) |>
  mutate(resp = factor(resp, c(
    "Temperature", "Coral", "Fleshy Macroalgae", "Herbivorous Fish",
    "Corallivore Fish", "Ecosystem Rd", "Ecosystem Pmax", "N stock"
  ))) |>
  mutate(pred = case_when(
    pred == "temperature" ~ "Temperature",
    pred == "mitemperature" ~ "Temperature",
    pred == "milogrd" ~ "Ecosystem Rd Rate",
    pred == "logcoral" ~ "Coral Cover",
    pred == "logfleshy" ~ "Fleshy Macroalgae Cover",
    pred == "Year" ~ "Year",
    pred == "yearresid" ~ "Non-Temperature Yearly Variability"
  )) |>
  mutate(pred = factor(pred, c(
    "Ecosystem Rd Rate", "Fleshy Macroalgae Cover",
    "Coral Cover", "Non-Temperature Yearly Variability",
    "Temperature", "Year"
  )))

gp_edges |>
  ggplot(aes(x = est, y = pred)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "firebrick", aes(alpha = sig)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, alpha = sig), height = 0, color = "firebrick") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  scale_alpha(range = c(0.6, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Standardized Effect Size",
    y = "Predictor Variables",
    title = "SEM Path Coefficients"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  facet_wrap(~resp, nrow = 1) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# Unscaling parameters
Yearmodelvalues <- Year_Averages |>
  mutate(
    logfleshy    = log(mean_fleshy),
    logproducers = log(mean_alive),
    logrd        = log(Rd),
    logpmax      = log(Pmax),
    N_percent    = log(N_percent),
    yearresid    = yearresid
  ) |>
  select(
    Year, meancoral = mean_coral, meanfleshy = mean_fleshy,
    temperature = Max_temp, flow = Flow_mean, Npercent = N_percent,

modelmean <- Yearmodelvalues |> summarise(across(everything(), mean, na.rm = TRUE))

# Year → Temperature
temp_year <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "temperature", effects = "Year")
ty_plot <- as_tibble(temp_year$temperature.temperature_Year) |>
  mutate(
    Year       = Year       * modelsd$Year        + modelmean$Year,
    estimate__ = estimate__ * modelsd$temperature + modelmean$temperature,
    lower__    = lower__    * modelsd$temperature + modelmean$temperature,
    upper__    = upper__    * modelsd$temperature + modelmean$temperature
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = 0.25, fill = "#67bed9") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = Year, y = Max_temp), alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Temperature (°C)", title = "Year → Temperature")

  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = mean_fleshy, y = Herbivores), alpha = 0.5) +
  coord_trans(x = "log") +
  labs(
    x = "Fleshy Macroalgae Cover (%)",
    y = expression(atop("Herbivore Fish Biomass", "(g m"^-2*")")),
    title = "Fleshy Algae → Herbivore Fish"
  )

# ── Row 4: Metabolism → ecosystem function ────────────────────────────────

# Respiration → N Content
N_Rd <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "Npercent", effects = "logrd")
nr_plot <- as_tibble(N_Rd$Npercent.Npercent_logrd) |>
  mutate(
    logrd      = exp(logrd      * modelsd$logrd    + modelmean$logrd),
    estimate__ = exp(estimate__ * modelsd$Npercent + modelmean$Npercent),
    lower__    = exp(lower__    * modelsd$Npercent + modelmean$Npercent),
    upper__    = exp(upper__    * modelsd$Npercent + modelmean$Npercent)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = logrd, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = 0.25, fill = "#67bed9") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = Rd, y = N_percent), alpha = 0.5) +
  coord_trans(x = "log", y = "log") +
  labs(
    x = expression("Ecosystem Respiration (mmol O"[2]*" m"^-2*" hr"^-1*")"),
    y = "Nitrogen Content (%)",
    title = "Respiration → Algal N Content"
  )

# Respiration → Ecosystem Pmax
rd_pmax <- conditional_effects(brms_sem_full, resp = "logpmax", effects = "logrd")
rp_plot <- as_tibble(rd_pmax$logpmax.logpmax_logrd) |>
  mutate(
    logrd      = exp(logrd      * modelsd$logrd   + modelmean$logrd),
    estimate__ = exp(estimate__ * modelsd$logpmax + modelmean$logpmax),
    lower__    = exp(lower__    * modelsd$logpmax + modelmean$logpmax),
    upper__    = exp(upper__    * modelsd$logpmax + modelmean$logpmax)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = logrd, y = estimate__)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__), alpha = 0.25, fill = "#67bed9") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = Year_Averages, aes(x = Rd, y = Pmax), alpha = 0.5) +
  coord_trans(x = "log", y = "log") +
  labs(
    x = expression("Ecosystem Respiration (mmol O"[2]*" m"^-2*" hr"^-1*")"),
    y = expression(atop("Ecosystem Pmax", "(mmol O"[2]*" m"^-2*" hr"^-1*")")),
    title = "Respiration → Ecosystem Pmax"
  )

(ty_plot | ct_plot) /

Ecosystem Projections

Code 
# z-log scale ceilings corresponding to 100% benthic cover.
# Both cover equations were fitted with trunc(ub = z_ceil) to respect the
# 0–100% biological bound. The same ceiling is applied in all projection
# matrices so that manual propagation is consistent with the SEM likelihood.
# Values are hardcoded (verified: back-transform to exactly 100% cover).
z_ceil_coral  <- 3.39   # (log(100) - mean(log(coral%))) / sd(log(coral%))
z_ceil_fleshy <- 2.26   # (log(100) - mean(log(fleshy%))) / sd(log(fleshy%))

Reduced SEM: Parsimonious Model

Three of the twelve pathways in the full SEM had 95% credible intervals spanning zero — direct temperature effects on respiration (β = 0.22, 95% CI −0.22 to 0.62), direct temperature effects on Pmax (β = −0.16, −0.78 to 0.45), and a direct coral effect on Pmax (β = −0.35, −1.40 to 0.71) — indicating that these pathways are not reliably supported by the data. Retaining them in projection creates two problems: the positive temperature→Rd coefficient generates a spurious upward push on Rd when temperature is extrapolated beyond the fitted range, and the large uncertainty on the coral→Pmax and temperature→Pmax terms inflates Pmax credible intervals. A reduced 9-pathway SEM was therefore fitted with these three terms removed.

Code 
# Reduced SEM: remove 3 non-significant pathways
#   1. Temperature → Rd (direct):      remove mi(temperature) from bf_logrd
#   2. Temperature → Pmax (direct):    remove mi(temperature) from bf_logpmax
#   3. Coral → Pmax (direct):          remove logcoral from bf_logpmax

bf_temp_r        <- bf(temperature | mi()             ~ 1 + Year)
bf_coraltemp_r   <- bf(logcoral    | trunc(ub = 3.39) ~ 1 + temperature + yearresid)
bf_logrd_r       <- bf(logrd       | mi()             ~ 1 + logcoral)
bf_logpmax_r     <- bf(logpmax     | mi()             ~ 1 + mi(logrd))
bf_fleshy_r      <- bf(logfleshy   | trunc(ub = 2.26) ~ logcoral)
bf_herbs_r       <- bf(herbs       | mi()             ~ 1 + logfleshy)
bf_corallivore_r <- bf(Corallivore | mi()             ~ 1 + logcoral)
bf_nutrients_r   <- bf(Npercent    | mi()             ~ 1 + mi(logrd))

brms_sem_reduced <- brm(
  bf_temp_r + bf_coraltemp_r + bf_logrd_r + bf_herbs_r + bf_corallivore_r +
    bf_nutrients_r + bf_fleshy_r + bf_logpmax_r + set_rescor(FALSE),
  data    = semdata2,
  chains  = 3, iter = 10000, warmup = 5000, seed = 11,
  sample_prior = "no",
  prior   = c(
    set_prior("normal(0, 2)",    class = "b"),
    set_prior("normal(0, 0.25)", resp = "temperature", class = "sigma", lb = 0),
    set_prior("normal(0, 2)",    class = "Intercept")
  ),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15),
  family  = gaussian(),
  silent = 2, refresh = 0
)

Code 
# Manual R² for mi()-imputed responses
for (resp in c("logrd", "logpmax")) {
  fit_f <- fitted(brms_sem_full,    resp = resp)[, "Estimate"]
  fit_r <- fitted(brms_sem_reduced, resp = resp)[, "Estimate"]
  obs_v <- semdata2[[resp]]
  ok    <- !is.na(obs_v)
  cat(sprintf("%-10s  Full R²: %.3f   Reduced R²: %.3f\n", resp,
              cor(fit_f[ok], obs_v[ok])^2, cor(fit_r[ok], obs_v[ok])^2))
}

Code 
set.seed(6214)
post_r <- as_draws_df(brms_sem_reduced) |> as_tibble() |> slice_sample(n = 3000)
n_r    <- nrow(post_r)

# yearresid matrix: observed for 2005-2025, zero for 2026-2055
yr_resid_vec_r <- sapply(proj_years, function(y) {
  row <- yr_resid_lookup |> filter(Year == y)
  if (nrow(row) == 1 && !is.na(row$yr)) row$yr else 0
})
yr_resid_mat_r <- matrix(rep(yr_resid_vec_r, each = n_r), nrow = n_r)
yr_mat_r       <- matrix(rep(year_std, each = n_r), nrow = n_r)

# ── Propagate reduced SEM causal chain ────────────────────────────────────────
temp_mat_r   <- rs(post_r$b_temperature_Year,     yr_mat_r)   + post_r$b_temperature_Intercept
coral_mat_r  <- rs(post_r$b_logcoral_temperature, temp_mat_r) +
                rs(post_r$b_logcoral_yearresid,   yr_resid_mat_r) +
                post_r$b_logcoral_Intercept
rd_mat_r     <- rs(post_r$b_logrd_logcoral, coral_mat_r)      + post_r$b_logrd_Intercept
fleshy_mat_r <- pmin(rs(post_r$b_logfleshy_logcoral, coral_mat_r) + post_r$b_logfleshy_Intercept,
                     z_ceil_fleshy)
cov_mat_r    <- rs(post_r$b_Corallivore_logcoral, coral_mat_r)+ post_r$b_Corallivore_Intercept
herb_mat_r   <- rs(post_r$b_herbs_logfleshy, fleshy_mat_r)    + post_r$b_herbs_Intercept
pmax_mat_r   <- rs(post_r$bsp_logpmax_milogrd, rd_mat_r)      + post_r$b_logpmax_Intercept
n_mat_r      <- rs(post_r$bsp_Npercent_milogrd, rd_mat_r)     + post_r$b_Npercent_Intercept

proj_list_r <- list(
  Temperature    = bt_lin(temp_mat_r,   modelmean$temperature, modelsd$temperature),
  `Coral Cover`  = bt_log(coral_mat_r,  modelmean$logcoral,    modelsd$logcoral),
  Respiration    = bt_log(rd_mat_r,     modelmean$logrd,       modelsd$logrd),
  `Fleshy Algae` = bt_log(fleshy_mat_r, modelmean$logfleshy,   modelsd$logfleshy),
  Pmax           = bt_log(pmax_mat_r,   modelmean$logpmax,     modelsd$logpmax),
  `N Content`    = bt_log(n_mat_r,
                          mean(log(Year_Averages$N_percent), na.rm = TRUE),
                          sd(log(Year_Averages$N_percent),   na.rm = TRUE))
)
proj_list_r[["P:R Ratio"]] <- proj_list_r$Pmax / proj_list_r$Respiration

proj_tbl_r <- imap_dfr(proj_list_r, function(mat, vname) {
  tibble(variable = vname, Year = rep(proj_years, each = n_r), value = as.vector(mat)) |>
    group_by(variable, Year) |>
    summarise(median = median(value),
              lo95 = quantile(value, .025), hi95 = quantile(value, .975),
              lo50 = quantile(value, .25),  hi50 = quantile(value, .75),
              .groups = "drop")
})

# ── Counterfactual: temperature stabilised at 2025 ────────────────────────────
# temp_2025_std: z-standardised 2025 annual maximum temperature
# = (observed 2025 max temp - SEM temperature mean) / SEM temperature SD
temp_2025_std <- (Year_Averages$Max_temp[Year_Averages$Year == 2025] -
                    modelmean$temperature) / modelsd$temperature
temp_mat_r_cf <- temp_mat_r
temp_mat_r_cf[, which(proj_years > 2025)] <- temp_2025_std

coral_mat_r_cf  <- rs(post_r$b_logcoral_temperature, temp_mat_r_cf)   +
                   rs(post_r$b_logcoral_yearresid,   yr_resid_mat_r)  +
                   post_r$b_logcoral_Intercept
rd_mat_r_cf     <- rs(post_r$b_logrd_logcoral, coral_mat_r_cf)        + post_r$b_logrd_Intercept
fleshy_mat_r_cf <- pmin(rs(post_r$b_logfleshy_logcoral, coral_mat_r_cf) + post_r$b_logfleshy_Intercept,
                        z_ceil_fleshy)
pmax_mat_r_cf   <- rs(post_r$bsp_logpmax_milogrd, rd_mat_r_cf)        + post_r$b_logpmax_Intercept
n_mat_r_cf      <- rs(post_r$bsp_Npercent_milogrd, rd_mat_r_cf)       + post_r$b_Npercent_Intercept

proj_tbl_r_cf <- imap_dfr(
  list(Temperature    = bt_lin(temp_mat_r_cf,   modelmean$temperature, modelsd$temperature),
       `Coral Cover`  = bt_log(coral_mat_r_cf,  modelmean$logcoral,    modelsd$logcoral),
       Respiration    = bt_log(rd_mat_r_cf,     modelmean$logrd,       modelsd$logrd),
       `Fleshy Algae` = bt_log(fleshy_mat_r_cf, modelmean$logfleshy,   modelsd$logfleshy),
       Pmax           = bt_log(pmax_mat_r_cf,   modelmean$logpmax,     modelsd$logpmax),
       `N Content`    = bt_log(n_mat_r_cf,
                               mean(log(Year_Averages$N_percent), na.rm = TRUE),
                               sd(log(Year_Averages$N_percent),   na.rm = TRUE))),
  function(mat, vname) {
    tibble(variable = vname, Year = rep(proj_years, each = n_r), value = as.vector(mat)) |>
      group_by(variable, Year) |>
      summarise(median = median(value),
                lo95 = quantile(value, .025), hi95 = quantile(value, .975),
                lo50 = quantile(value, .25),  hi50 = quantile(value, .75),
                .groups = "drop")
  })

Code 
# ── Propagate each SSP scenario × CMIP6 percentile through the reduced SEM ───
# Approach: two-phase projection anchored to the 2025 OBSERVED ecosystem state.
#   Phase 1 (2005–2025): observed z-scores from semdata2 used directly where
#     available, overriding the SEM chain prediction column-by-column. This
#     ensures the historical lines track the actual data rather than the
#     amplified sequential prediction. 2005 (not in semdata2) uses SEM prediction.
#   Phase 2 (2026–2100): delta method. Only the CHANGE in temperature from the
#     scenario's CMIP6 2025 value is propagated through the SEM path coefficients,
#     starting from the 2025 observed ecosystem state. This preserves the real
#     2025 coral, fleshy algae, and metabolism values as the projection origin.

# ── Observed z-score lookup (built once, reused across all propagation calls) ──
obs_anchors <- semdata2 |>
  mutate(Year_actual = round(Year * modelsd$Year + modelmean$Year)) |>
  select(Year_actual, logcoral, logrd, logfleshy, logpmax, Npercent, yearresid)

propagate_wb_ssp <- function(scenario_name, pct = "median") {
  # ── CMIP6 temperatures, z-scored, 2005–2100 (96 values) ──────────────────
  temps_bc <- wb_proj_bc |>
    filter(scenario == scenario_name, percentile == pct) |>
    arrange(year) |>
    pull(tasmax_bc)

  temp_z <- (temps_bc - modelmean$temperature) / modelsd$temperature

  n_hist <- 21L; n_proj <- 75L

  # ── Phase 1: SEM chain (fallback values for years/variables missing obs) ──
  temp_z_hist <- temp_z[seq_len(n_hist)]
  tm_hist <- matrix(rep(temp_z_hist, each = n_r), nrow = n_r)

  yr_rv_hist <- sapply(2005:2025, function(y) {
    row <- yr_resid_lookup |> filter(Year == y)
    if (nrow(row) == 1L && !is.na(row$yr)) row$yr else 0
  })
  yrm_hist <- matrix(rep(yr_rv_hist, each = n_r), nrow = n_r)

  cm_hist <- pmin(rs(post_r$b_logcoral_temperature, tm_hist) +
                  rs(post_r$b_logcoral_yearresid,   yrm_hist) +
                  post_r$b_logcoral_Intercept,  z_ceil_coral)
  rm_hist <- rs(post_r$b_logrd_logcoral,          cm_hist) + post_r$b_logrd_Intercept
  fm_hist <- pmin(rs(post_r$b_logfleshy_logcoral, cm_hist) +
                  post_r$b_logfleshy_Intercept, z_ceil_fleshy)
  pm_hist <- rs(post_r$bsp_logpmax_milogrd,  rm_hist) + post_r$b_logpmax_Intercept
  nm_hist <- rs(post_r$bsp_Npercent_milogrd, rm_hist) + post_r$b_Npercent_Intercept

  # ── Override historical columns with observed z-scores where available ────
  obs_z <- function(y, col) {
    row <- obs_anchors |> filter(Year_actual == y)
    if (nrow(row) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
    v <- row[[col]][[1L]]
    if (is.na(v)) NA_real_ else v
  }

  for (j in 2:n_hist) {          # j = 1 → 2005 (not in semdata2, keep SEM)
    y <- 2004L + j
    oc <- obs_z(y, "logcoral");  if (!is.na(oc)) cm_hist[, j] <- oc
    or <- obs_z(y, "logrd");     if (!is.na(or)) rm_hist[, j] <- or
    of <- obs_z(y, "logfleshy"); if (!is.na(of)) fm_hist[, j] <- of
    op <- obs_z(y, "logpmax");   if (!is.na(op)) pm_hist[, j] <- op
    on <- obs_z(y, "Npercent");  if (!is.na(on)) nm_hist[, j] <- on
  }

  # ── 2025 observed anchor (scalar per variable) ────────────────────────────
  z25 <- obs_anchors |> filter(Year_actual == 2025L) |> slice(1)
  c25 <- z25$logcoral
  r25 <- z25$logrd
  f25 <- z25$logfleshy
  p25 <- z25$logpmax
  # N_percent NA in 2025: impute from observed Rd via SEM median
  n25 <- median(post_r$bsp_Npercent_milogrd * r25 + post_r$b_Npercent_Intercept)

  # ── Phase 2 (2026–2100): delta from 2025 observed anchor ─────────────────
  temp_z_2025 <- temp_z[n_hist]
  delta_temp  <- temp_z[(n_hist + 1L):(n_hist + n_proj)] - temp_z_2025
  dtm         <- matrix(rep(delta_temp, each = n_r), nrow = n_r)  # n_r × n_proj

  cm_proj <- pmin(c25 + rs(post_r$b_logcoral_temperature, dtm), z_ceil_coral)
  dcm     <- cm_proj - c25
  rm_proj <- r25 + rs(post_r$b_logrd_logcoral,          dcm)
  fm_proj <- pmin(f25 + rs(post_r$b_logfleshy_logcoral, dcm), z_ceil_fleshy)
  drm     <- rm_proj - r25
  pm_proj <- p25 + rs(post_r$bsp_logpmax_milogrd,  drm)
  nm_proj <- n25 + rs(post_r$bsp_Npercent_milogrd, drm)

  # ── Combine & back-transform ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  tm <- matrix(rep(temp_z, each = n_r), nrow = n_r)
  cm <- cbind(cm_hist, cm_proj);  rm <- cbind(rm_hist, rm_proj)
  fm <- cbind(fm_hist, fm_proj);  pm <- cbind(pm_hist, pm_proj)
  nm <- cbind(nm_hist, nm_proj)

  imap_dfr(
    list(Temperature    = bt_lin(tm, modelmean$temperature, modelsd$temperature),
         `Coral Cover`  = bt_log(cm, modelmean$logcoral,    modelsd$logcoral),
         Respiration    = bt_log(rm, modelmean$logrd,       modelsd$logrd),
         `Fleshy Algae` = bt_log(fm, modelmean$logfleshy,   modelsd$logfleshy),
         Pmax           = bt_log(pm, modelmean$logpmax,     modelsd$logpmax),
         `N Content`    = bt_log(nm,
                                  mean(log(Year_Averages$N_percent), na.rm = TRUE),
                                  sd(log(Year_Averages$N_percent),   na.rm = TRUE))),
    function(mat, vname) {
      tibble(scenario = scenario_name, percentile = pct, variable = vname,
             year = rep(2005:2100, each = n_r), value = as.vector(mat)) |>
        group_by(scenario, percentile, variable, year) |>
        summarise(median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
                  lo95   = quantile(value, .025, na.rm = TRUE),
                  hi95   = quantile(value, .975, na.rm = TRUE),
                  lo50   = quantile(value, .25,  na.rm = TRUE),
                  hi50   = quantile(value, .75,  na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop")
    })
}

wb_all_combos <- expand_grid(
  scenario   = c("ssp126", "ssp245", "ssp585"),
  percentile = c("p10", "median", "p90")
)
wb_proj_tbl <- bind_rows(
  mapply(propagate_wb_ssp,
         scenario_name = wb_all_combos$scenario,
         pct           = wb_all_combos$percentile,
         SIMPLIFY      = FALSE)
)

# ── Tidy for plotting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
wb_sem_ci_band <- wb_proj_tbl |>
  filter(percentile == "median") |>
  select(scenario, variable, year, central = median, lo_sem = lo95, hi_sem = hi95)

wb_clim_band <- wb_proj_tbl |>
  filter(percentile %in% c("p10", "p90")) |>
  select(scenario, variable, year, percentile, clim_med = median) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = percentile, values_from = clim_med) |>
  rename(lo_clim = p10, hi_clim = p90)

wb_ssp_labels  <- c(ssp126 = "SSP1-2.6", ssp245 = "SSP2-4.5", ssp585 = "SSP5-8.5")
wb_ssp_colours <- c(ssp126 = "#2196F3",  ssp245 = "#FF9800",   ssp585 = "#E53935")
wb_var_order   <- c("Temperature","Coral Cover","Respiration",
                    "Fleshy Algae","Pmax","N Content")
wb_var_units   <- c(Temperature    = "\u00b0C",
                    `Coral Cover`  = "% cover",
                    Respiration    = "mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 hr\u207b\u00b9",
                    `Fleshy Algae` = "% cover",
                    Pmax           = "mmol O\u2082 m\u207b\u00b2 hr\u207b\u00b9",
                    `N Content`    = "% N")

wb_plot_tbl <- wb_sem_ci_band |>
  left_join(wb_clim_band, by = c("scenario", "variable", "year")) |>
  mutate(variable       = factor(variable, levels = wb_var_order),
         scenario_label = wb_ssp_labels[scenario])

# ── Historical temperature spread: inter-model p10/p90 across CDS CMIP6 ensemble ─
# For 2005-2014 (historical period), the SSP ensemble spread is not defined;
# use the CMIP6 historical run inter-model spread (p10–p90 across 10 bias-corrected
# CDS CMIP6 models) to fill the outer uncertainty ribbon for the Temperature panel.
om_hist_spread <- ann_cmip6_bc |>
  filter(year %in% 2005:2014) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(lo_clim_om = quantile(ann_max_bc, 0.10),
            hi_clim_om = quantile(ann_max_bc, 0.90),
            .groups = "drop")

wb_plot_tbl <- wb_plot_tbl |>
  left_join(om_hist_spread, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    lo_clim = if_else(variable == "Temperature" & year %in% 2005:2014,
                      lo_clim_om, lo_clim),
    hi_clim = if_else(variable == "Temperature" & year %in% 2005:2014,
                      hi_clim_om, hi_clim)
  ) |>
  select(-lo_clim_om, -hi_clim_om)
Code 
wb_y_limits <- list(
  Temperature    = NULL,
  `Coral Cover`  = c(0, NA),
  Respiration    = c(0, NA),
  `Fleshy Algae` = c(0, 100),
  Pmax           = c(60, NA),
  `N Content`    = c(0.3, NA)
)

make_wb_panel <- function(vname) {
  d_v   <- wb_plot_tbl |> filter(variable == vname)
  obs_v <- Year_Averages |>
    select(year = Year,
           Temperature    = Max_temp,
           `Coral Cover`  = mean_coral,
           Respiration    = Rd,
           `Fleshy Algae` = mean_fleshy,
           Pmax           = Pmax,
           `N Content`    = N_percent) |>
    pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "variable", values_to = "obs") |>
    filter(variable == vname)
  unit <- wb_var_units[[vname]]
  ylim <- wb_y_limits[[vname]]

  # Ribbons only in the projection period (2026+), where uncertainty is meaningful.
  # For temperature, the outer (climate) ribbon also shows the CMIP6 model spread
  # in the historical period (outer ribbon is valid there).
  # For other variables, ribbons in 2005-2025 are artefacts: 2005 uses the SEM
  # chain (very wide), observed years collapse to zero width, and the outer ribbon
  # is inverted for variables with a negative temperature relationship.
  d_ribbon       <- d_v |> filter(year > 2025)
  d_clim_ribbon  <- if (vname == "Temperature") d_v else d_ribbon

  p <- ggplot(d_v, aes(x = year, colour = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 2025.5, xmax = 2100, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "grey92", alpha = .6) +
    geom_ribbon(data = d_clim_ribbon,
                aes(ymin = pmin(lo_clim, hi_clim), ymax = pmax(lo_clim, hi_clim)),
                alpha = 0.10, colour = NA) +
    geom_ribbon(data = d_ribbon,
                aes(ymin = lo_sem, ymax = hi_sem),
                alpha = 0.20, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(aes(y = central), linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(data = obs_v, aes(x = year, y = obs),
               colour = "black", size = 1.5, shape = 21, fill = "white",
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 2025.5, linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "grey50", linewidth = .4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = wb_ssp_colours, labels = wb_ssp_labels, name = "Scenario") +
    scale_fill_manual(  values = wb_ssp_colours, labels = wb_ssp_labels, name = "Scenario") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2100, 20)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = unit, title = vname) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          plot.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  if (!is.null(ylim)) p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim)
  if (vname == "Fleshy Algae")
    p <- p + annotate("text", x = 2060, y = 96,
                      label = "100% ceiling", size = 2.3, colour = "grey40",
                      hjust = 0.5, fontface = "italic")
  p
}

wb_panels <- lapply(wb_var_order, make_wb_panel)

wb_legend_plot <- ggplot(
  wb_plot_tbl |> filter(variable == "Temperature"),
  aes(x = year, y = central, colour = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo_sem, ymax = hi_sem), alpha = .25, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = .9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = wb_ssp_colours, labels = wb_ssp_labels,
                      name = "CMIP6 Scenario") +
  scale_fill_manual(  values = wb_ssp_colours, labels = wb_ssp_labels,
                      name = "CMIP6 Scenario") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.5))) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.direction = "vertical",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 8))
wb_leg <- cowplot::get_legend(wb_legend_plot)

wb_main <- wrap_plots(wb_panels, ncol = 2) & theme(legend.position = "none")
cowplot::plot_grid(wb_main, wb_leg, ncol = 2, rel_widths = c(1, 0.12))
